newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand's 1996 exports seen growing five pct.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's 1996 exports seen growing five pct.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viranwan said on Monday he expected Thailand's 1996 exports to grow no more than 5.0 percent compared with robust 23.6 percent growth in 1995.
"I am not sure that the export growth for the whole year will be higher than 5.0 percent because the export growth in the first eight months was only 3.1 percent," he told reporters.
"The slower export growth will not have a serious impact on the Thai economy. The sluggish export situation has occured throughout the region," he said.
Foreign investors and economists have been concerned about the sharply slower Thai export growth anticipated for this year.
Amnuay, who supervises the outgoing administration's economic policies, was speaking after a meeting of a government panel charged with monitoring Thailand's economic performance.
Elections to replace the current government led by caretaker Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa will be held on November 17.
Amnuay said total exports in the first eight months were 930 billion baht ($37.2 billion), or 3.1 percent higher than that recorded in the same period last year.
Thailand's exports in 1995 totalled 1.38 trillion baht, he added.
The Bank of Thailand recently set the 1996 exports growth target at 10.2 percent.
